text:
matt: FYI canary finished ~09:12 and we're seeing a p99 tail spike on tiny-seq (<=16) requests after the runtime push. p50 fine, throughput fine, tail jumped ~8-12x.

deploy-bot: deploy redwood/runtime@release-2026.03.17 finished in cluster-3 (canary=5%).

alex: grabbing perf graphs now. do we have a diff for kernel selector or batching heuristics in this rollout?

maria: quick skim: the autotune change flipped a threshold that rebinds tiny sequences to the new 'vector-dense-kernel' when microbatch>1. previous selector kept them on 'scalar-smallseq' with special kv-cache path.

priya: confirmed in canary logs - selector.tune: threshold_microbatch=2 -> 1 in this rollout. that caused kernel_autoselect to choose vector-dense for many tiny requests.

matt: that matches what we're seeing. vector-dense has better throughput for larger seq but terrible cold-kv hit behavior for tiny seq, plus its prefetch path increases tail due to expensive init.

alex: can you paste the config diff?

maria: here, from the release PR: 

```diff
- selector.threshold.microbatch: 2
+ selector.threshold.microbatch: 1
```

maria: and an excerpt from autotune logic: 

```py
if observed_microbatch >= selector.threshold.microbatch:
    bind_kernel('vector-dense-kernel')
else:
    bind_kernel('scalar-smallseq')
```

tony: we also changed kv-cache warmup ordering in the same change set (prefetch queue prioritized after kernel bind). that might magnify the initial spike.

priya: rolling a quick canary-level rollback to revert threshold to 2. initiating revert now.

matt: thanks. can we also temporarily disable the prefetch reorder? put it behind a flag.

priya: done. patch rolled: selector.threshold.microbatch=2 + prefetch.reorder=false. rollback applied to canary.

deploy-bot: rollback redwood/runtime@release-2026.03.17 -> redwood/runtime@release-2026.03.16 applied to cluster-3 (canary).

alex: watching metrics... p99 for tiny-seq back to baseline in ~40s. tail gone. CPU and GPU utilization steady.

matt: great. action items: 1) revert the autotune threshold change from the feature branch until we have microbench evidence for tiny seq; 2) add a conservative kv-cache warmup path for smallseq kernels; 3) add a canary test that drives tiny-seq workloads at burst concurrency and checks p95/p99 tail.

maria: logging the regression root cause as 'kernel-selector threshold flip + prefetch reorder' and linking perf graphs + canary logs to the PR. will open follow-up with benchmarking script.

priya: opened follow-up issue: https://redwood.internal/issue/RT-4823 (attachments: perf-graphs, selector-logs).

tony: note for postmortem: this is a classic SLO vs throughput tradeoff — autotune optimized for throughput without evaluating tail for tiny sequences. add regression tests to prevent selector flips that harm p99.

matt: agree. also adjust alerting: add a short-window p99 alarm for tiny-seq route that triggers before full canary completes.

alex: i'll draft a test harness that runs microbench workloads (seq=4..32, conc=1..16) and compares kernel binding choices vs p99. will include kv-cache priming scenarios.

matt: thanks team. marking this thread resolved after postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:

maria: closing the canary ticket, will keep the branch open for validated rework.

priya: last note: if anyone sees residual tail on other routes ping me directly.

tony: :thumbsup:
